question: Does proximity to the owner differ by odour condition, and does the answer depend on whether dogs or time bins are counted?
claim: Averaging the 24 dogs into 12 time-bin means turns p = 0.23 into p = 9.6e-06
n_observations: left panel draws the 36 condition x time-bin means the published tests used ({'blank': 12, 'joy': 12, 'stress': 12}); right panel draws one point per dog
error_bar: mean with 95% CI over dogs, n = {'blank': 6, 'joy': 9, 'stress': 9} (right panel); mean with 95% CI over the 12 time bins (left panel); both definitions are printed inside the figure
transformations: per-dog value is the mean over that dog's coded 5-second bins

y.units: fraction of the dog's coded sample points at which it was nearest the owner

shared_scales: yes; both panels share the y axis limits and ticks

color.redundant_with: x position and x tick label

excluded: of 43 recruited dogs, 14 never reached Part 2, 3 discontinued and 2 did not investigate the odour, leaving 24 (blank 6, joy 9, stress 9); the paper does not attribute the 2 excluded dogs to a condition, so per-group entry counts are not recoverable and the figure says so
missing: 4 dogs have 11 coded sample points rather than 12; those bins are dropped from that dog's mean and the denominator is stated on the figure
